title: Transactional atomicity: multi-statement writes through a transaction helper roll back on any error
description: Multi-statement writes that require atomicity are issued through the facade's transaction helper owned on TAC-2803-persistence-data-postgres-transaction-helper.interfaces.withTransaction. The helper wraps the transaction-control primitives named there around a consumer callback, awaits the callback's statements (each issued through the prepared-statement discipline in REQ-003), commits on the callback's successful completion, and rolls back with a transactionRolledBack lifecycle event on any statement failure inside the callback (including a constraint violation the driver surfaces as an error). The lifecycle event carries the failing statement's zero-based index inside the callback. The helper does not swallow the underlying error; it re-throws after the rollback so the caller observes the failure and the facade's own error boundary constructs the internal error record.
rationale: Postgres MVCC gives transactions a clean rollback surface; the helper's job is to make the rollback observable and to guarantee no partial commit lands on the shipped database. The zero-based statement index on the event is what lets the calling code (or a log line, or an error boundary) name which statement failed inside a batch of five without a stack-trace decode.
